quote: Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

earliest.work: Knoxville, Tennessee newspaper report on an Al-Anon meeting

notes: Probably from a twelve-step community; no single author is known. Credited to Einstein by 1990 (Austin American-Statesman), long after his death.

quote: Be the change you wish to see in the world.

earliest.author: Arleen Lorrance
earliest.work: Book chapter in Developing Priorities and a Style: Selected Readings in Education for Teachers and Parents
earliest.wording: Be the change you want to see happen

notes: Gandhi wrote a related but much longer passage in 1913. Quote Investigator credits Lorrance with the saying.

quote: The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing.

earliest.author: Charles F. Aked
earliest.work: Speech calling for restrictions on alcohol, quoted in print
earliest.wording: It has been said that for evil men to accomplish their purpose it is only necessary that good men should do nothing.

notes: Burke and John Stuart Mill (1867) wrote related ideas, but not this wording. R. Murray Hyslop credited the modern version to Burke in July 1920.

earliest.author: Laurel Thatcher Ulrich
earliest.work: Vertuous Women Found: New England Ministerial Literature, 1668-1735 (American Quarterly 28:1)

notes: Published in the Spring 1976 issue of an academic journal. Ulrich later used the line as a book title (2007).

quote: If I had asked people what they wanted, they would have said faster horses.

earliest.work: Letter from David Lowings in Marketing Week
earliest.wording: If I had asked my customers what they wanted they would have said a faster horse

notes: No good evidence that Ford said it; he died in 1947. A 1999 cruise industry article imagined what Ford's customers would have asked for, without quoting him.

quote: Everybody is a genius. But if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will live its whole life believing that it is stupid.

earliest.work: The Rhythm of Life: Living Every Day with Passion and Purpose by Matthew Kelly

notes: The earliest close match already credits Einstein, decades after his death. Older animal-school fables carry the same idea.

quote: I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it.

earliest.author: Evelyn Beatrice Hall (as S. G. Tallentyre)
earliest.wording: I disapprove of what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it

notes: Hall wrote it as a summary of Voltaire's attitude. It has never been found in Voltaire's own works.

quote: Twenty years from now you will be more disappointed by the things you didn't do than by the ones you did do.

earliest.author: Sarah Frances Brown
earliest.work: P.S. I Love You by H. Jackson Brown Jr.

notes: Brown's book collected his mother's advice. A New Yorker advert in April 1998 labelled it as attributed to Mark Twain.

quote: Whether you think you can, or you think you can't, you're right.

earliest.author: Henry Ford (as credited by The Reader's Digest)
earliest.wording: Whether you believe you can do a thing or not, you are right.

notes: The idea circulated in looser forms for decades, including a 1940 locker-room sign. The 1947 Ford credit gave no source, so the link is likely but not certain.

quote: Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts.

earliest.author: William Bruce Cameron
earliest.work: Informal Sociology: A Casual Introduction to Sociological Thinking
earliest.wording: not everything that can be counted counts, and not everything that counts can be counted

notes: Cameron combined two phrases into the full saying, after Einstein's death.

quote: Do not go where the path may lead, go instead where there is no path and leave a trail.

earliest.author: Muriel Strode
earliest.work: Wind-Wafted Wild Flowers, in The Open Court
earliest.wording: I will not follow where the path may lead, but I will go where there is no path, and I will leave a trail.

notes: No source has been found in Emerson's works. Quote Investigator tentatively credits Strode.

quote: 640K ought to be enough for anyone.

earliest.work: InfoWorld editorial by James E. Fawcette
earliest.wording: When we set the upper limit of PC-DOS at 640K, we thought nobody would ever need that much memory.

notes: The 1985 editorial credited the idea to Gates with no precise source. Gates denied saying it in 1996, and the popular 1981 date has no support.
Rousseau put the words in the mouth of an unnamed great princess. He wrote this when Marie Antoinette was 11 and not yet married to Louis XVI.

quote: Gel, gel, ne olursan ol yine gel

earliest.author: Ebu Said Ebu'l-Hayr
earliest.wording: Gene gel, gene gel! Her ne olursan ol, gene gel

notes: Come, come, whatever you are, come again. Historian Murat Bardakci (2014) credits Ebu Said Ebu'l-Hayr, who lived about three centuries before Mevlana, but the authorship of Ebu Said's own poems is also uncertain.

quote: Genius is one percent inspiration, ninety-nine percent perspiration.
notes: Edison used both a 2-to-98 and a 1-to-99 ratio, and Quote Investigator says crediting him is reasonable. Similar ideas were already in circulation by 1892.
